decision_conditions:
To sustain, and enhance, local tree cover and amenity provision, replanting is required for removal of this Yew tree, with the same Species. Yew - Taxus baccata. 

In this respect, you are required to replant within 12 months of removal with one nursery grown, container grown stock trees of a minimum size of 3m in height and 10cm girth at the time of planting. This is known commonly as size 'standard' from tree nurseries.

If within a period of 5 years from the date of planting that tree or any tree planted in replacement for it, is removed, uprooted, destroyed or dies (or becomes in the opinion of the local planning authority seriously damaged) then the tree shall be replaced to reflect the specification of the approved planting scheme in the next available planting season or in accordance with a timetable agreed in writing with the local planning authority.

The tree must be planted in accordance with the Code of Practice for General Landscape Operations BS4428 1989 and  BS 8545:2014 Trees: from nursery to independence in the landscape recommendations. Reasonably 

Trees must be watered throughout the growing season (April to October) ideally with rainwater to field capacity to ensure establishment.  Trees should be mulched to reduce competition for water and soil drying.  Stake and tie maintenance should be undertaken as required but support checked during each visit.''
application_type_full: Tree works: Trees in conservation areas/subject to TPOs
description:
1001 Yew (tree 60, conifer of TPO T0028) Fell due to unsafe condition and rapid advance of decay. Replace with one yew tree in alternative location within churchyard.

Amended to 5 day Dead/dangerous notification.
'During the passage of Storm Austen on Friday, the stem suffered further damage and is now flexing such that the vertically aligned cracks on the south side of the stem are opening and closing in the wind. The complex of cracks and cavity openings extend from the bole to ground level meaning that the stem has now split open on its southern aspect and has lost structural integrity. The tree has therefore comfortably passed the safe limit for retention and has undergone primary stem failure. THREATS now indicates that the tree should be removed immediately without waiting for determination of the TPO application currently before you. The churchyard has been temporarily closed but I understand that members of the public are still entering the danger zone so there really is a high degree of urgency here.'
